item.title: Earthquake Surge: Indonesia 7.4 Tremor, Bay Area Jolt, and What They Mean for 2026
item.description:
The earth has been restless. In the span of just 48 hours, a 7.4-magnitude earthquake rocked Indonesian waters, a 4.9-magnitude quake jolted the San Francisco Bay Area awake, and seismologists in Japan issued warnings about ongoing large earthquake risks. Are we seeing a pattern — or is this just how our planet works?

Key Takeaways

  • A major 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck near Ternate, Indonesia on April 1, 2026, triggering a tsunami warning that was later lifted.
  • A 4.9-magnitude earthquake shook the Bay Area near Santa Cruz County in the early morning hours of April 2, 2026.
  • A rare 3.9-magnitude quake was detected in the Gulf of Mexico on March 30 — an unusual location for seismic activity.
  • New University of Washington research on the Cascadia Subduction Zone reveals fluid dynamics that could influence how the Pacific Northwest responds to a major quake.

Indonesia Earthquake: 7.4 Magnitude Triggers Tsunami Alert

On April 1, 2026, a powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck in Indonesian waters at 7:48 a.m. Eastern Indonesia time, approximately 79 miles northwest of Ternate, according to the United States Geological Survey (USGS).

item.title: Rocket Launch Today: Your Ultimate Guide to This Week's Space Missions
item.description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 just lit up the Florida sky on March 22, and at least four more launches are lined up before the month ends. If you’ve been searching “rocket launch today,” you’re in the right place.

Quick Summary

  • March 22: SpaceX launched 29 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral (completed)
  • March 24: Starlink Group 17-17 scheduled from Vandenberg, CA
  • March 26: Starlink Group 10-44 from Cape Canaveral, FL
  • March 29: Atlas V carrying Amazon Kuiper satellites + SpaceX Transporter 16 rideshare
  • Also this week: Roscosmos Progress 94 cargo spacecraft docking to the ISS

Rocket Launch Schedule: What’s Flying This Week

The final week of March 2026 is packed. SpaceX alone has three Falcon 9 flights on the calendar, and United Launch Alliance is preparing a significant Atlas V mission for Amazon’s satellite internet constellation.

item.title: Moon Mission Update: NASA's Artemis II Rocket Returns to Launch Pad for Historic April Liftoff
item.description:
For the first time in over half a century, astronauts are about to fly around the moon — and the rocket that will carry them just rolled back to the launch pad.

NASA moved its towering Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft back to Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center on March 20, 2026, setting the stage for an April 1 launch window. The four-person crew has already entered quarantine in Houston.
